chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Mutamatti' who had intercourse with his wife and had not yet performed the Ziyarah (of the Imam's shrine). He said: 'He should sacrifice a camel, and I fear that his Hajj has been broken if he was knowing, and if he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him.'

And I asked him about a man who had intercourse with his wife before he performed the Tawaf al-Nisa' (Circumambulation of the Women). He said: 'Upon him is a fat camel, and if he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him.'
He said: 'And I asked him about a man who kissed his wife and he had performed the Tawaf al-Nisa' but she had not performed it. He said: 'Upon him is blood (dam) which he would spill from himself.'

key_terms.جَزُورٌ: A camel (used as a sacrificial animal)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Dam; a blood sacrifice, typically a sheep or goat
key_terms.زُرْ: Ziyarah; visiting the shrine of the Imam or Prophet
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa'; the final circumambulation of the Kaaba performed by the pilgrim
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in the same season

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who has intercourse with his wife before completing the Ziyarah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific expiations (kaffarah) for a pilgrim in Ihram who engages in sexual intimacy with his wife, distinguishing penalties based on the ritual stage and the pilgrim's knowledge. It highlights the scholarly nuance that while ignorance may exempt one from the penalty in some cases, it does not necessarily invalidate the Hajj itself, reflecting the Imami approach to balancing ritual integrity with human fallibility. The text underscores the importance of precise ritual timing, as the severity of the penalty varies depending on whether the act occurred before or after Tawaf al-Nisa'.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about (a man) performing Tumutto falling upon his wife and he has not performed Ziyaarat. Heasws said: ‘He should sacrifice a camel, and Iasws fear that his Hajj would break if he was knowing; and if he was ignorant, so there is nothing upon him’.

And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who falls upon his wife before he has circumambulated the circumambulation of the women (طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is a fat camel. And, if he was ignorant, so there is nothing upon him’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who kisses his wife and he has circumambulated the circumambulation of the women (طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ), but she had not circumambulated. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is blood he would be spilling (of a sacrificial animal) from him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) and is involved in sexual intercourse with his wife before performing Tawaf of Ziyarat. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must offer Jazur (slaughter a camel), and I am afraid for his al-Hajj becoming invalid if he knows the rules; but if he does not know the rules there is nothing on him.’

I asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is involved in sexual intercourse with his wife before performing Tawaf al-Nisa’. He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes one healthy Jazur, but if he does not know the rules there is nothing on him.’
I then asked about a man who has completed Tawaf al-Nisa’ and kisses his wife who has not completed Tawaf al-Nisa’. He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes one animal offering.’”
